fields.title: 1. Event ① — The CEO's "Government Under 10% of Revenue" Remark, and the Filing Facts It Revealed
fields.md:
### 1-1. The Remark Itself (Candidate Table Only)

| Date (US) | Content | Source grade · source |
|---|---|---|
| **2026-11-06 (Fri)** | CEO X post (replying to Warren Redlich): government agency payments are **under 10% of SpaceX revenue this quarter (4Q26)** and **under 5% in about 1 year** · 3Q was **16.6%**, 2025 was **about 1/5** · government contracts are "BOTH the best product AND the lowest price!" · "Happy to cancel any that the government doesn't want. Just say the word!" · stock +6.05% ($131.09) at the time of the post | ⑤ Bloomberg report (original not read) → ⑥ [Investing.com 11/06 (reprinted by Yahoo)](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/spacex-government-contracts-under-10-183013206.html) · [Dallas Express 11/06](https://dallasexpress.com/national/just-say-the-word-musk-offers-to-cancel-unwanted-spacex-contracts/) · [TNW 11/06](https://thenextweb.com/news/spacex-government-revenue-under-10-percent-musk-anthropic) — original X post not read |
| 2026-11-03~04 | Midterm elections — ABC and others reported Democratic majorities in the House and Senate as "projected," not a confirmed count (Georgia runoff 12/1). The CEO's remark came right after this result, and Bloomberg wrote of "possible tension with the new Congress" (reported) | ⑥ [ABC7 11/04](https://abc7news.com/live-updates/midterm-elections-2026-live-updates-election-results-key-races-us/20001292/entry/20014313/) · [Al Jazeera results page](https://aljazeera.com/us-midterm-elections-2026/results/) |
| 2026-11-07 (detected 11/9 KST) | News watcher detected 2 bundles — **linked to T1 (4Q26 earnings)** | `data/spacex_watch.json` due |
| Filings | **No SpaceX 8-K or IR** — there is no filing document on the government revenue outlook or contract cancellation. The latest on EDGAR is the 11/06 8-K (Item 5.02, section 2); latest on the IR RSS is 11/06 | ① [EDGAR filing list](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json) · ② [IR RSS](https://ir.spacex.com/rss/pressrelease.aspx), checked 2026-11-09 |

**Arithmetic of the remark (not a verdict)**: If 3Q26 government revenue is about $2,419M (section 1-2) and stays flat in 4Q, then "under 10%" means **4Q revenue above $24.2 billion** (formula: 2,419 ÷ 0.10) — the same order of magnitude as the CFO's "year-end ARR $100 billion path" ($25 billion per quarter). So the remark reads as an increase in the **denominator (AI revenue)**, not a decline in government revenue. Either way, the customer concentration note in the 4Q26 10-K is the only filing checkpoint (T1). "Canceling unwanted contracts" is an intent; there is no filing of contract termination or amendment (8-K Item 1.02) (Source: table above · `state.musk_statements_as_milestone_candidates_only` 10/20 CFO remark · [8-K Ex.99.1 3Q26](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066482/spaceexplorationtechnologi.htm)).

### 1-2. The Revealed Fact — 10-Q "Customer A" Is the US Government (Correction)

| Fact | Value | Source grade · source |
|---|---|---|
| 10-Q concentration note (Note 3) — Customer A | **3Q26 16.6%** · 3Q25 23.9% · 9M26 17.3% · 9M25 21.6% · "Revenue from Customer A relates to **all three segments**" · Customer B (SI) 3Q26 34.5% · "no other customer exceeded 10%" · one receivables customer 27.7% | ① [10-Q R12](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R12.htm) · [10-Q body Note 3](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/spcx-20260930.htm) — customer names are not given |
| S-1 (2026-05-20) concentration disclosure — FY2025 | **US government 20.9%** (about $3.9 billion = 20.9% × $18,674M) · 2024 24.2% · 2023 25.2% · no other customer above 10% | ① S-1 original (10MB, not read this round) → ⑥ [spacex-ipo-dashboard (S-1 summary)](https://spacex-ipo-dashboard.vercel.app/) "Customer A (U.S. federal government) = 20.9% of 2025 revenue (~$3.9B)" · [Washington Technology 05/20](https://washingtontechnology.com/companies/2026/05/spacexs-s-1-lays-out-its-government-work-and-market-ambitions/413681/) "one-fifth of sales represents work for U.S. government agencies" |
| Figures in the CEO's 11/6 remark | "3Q 16.6%", "2025 about 1/5" — consistent with 10-Q Customer A and the S-1 US government share | ⑥ [Investing.com 11/06](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/spacex-government-contracts-under-10-183013206.html) — for cross-checking, not a basis for the verdict |
| Google contract (reported) | $920M per month = $2.76 billion per quarter = **18.9%** of 3Q26 revenue (formula: 2,760 ÷ 14,575) — at this size it would have been separately flagged as a customer above 10% → Google was under 10% in 3Q (before delivery milestones, T1) | ⑤ [TechCrunch 2026-06-05](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/05/google-will-pay-spacex-920m-per-month-for-compute/) · ① 10-Q R12 |

**Verdict**: Three lines point to the same place — ⓐ 9M25 21.6%, FY25 20.9% and 3Q25 23.9% form a continuous time series for one customer, and the S-1 called that customer the US government ⓑ "all three segments" fits a government buying launch (Space), Starshield (Connectivity) and government AI (SI), and does not fit the compute customer Google ⓒ the CEO himself said "government 16.6%." **Customer A = the US government.** The structure the November issue described as "both top-2 AI customers (Anthropic, Google) have a 2027-1H termination option" should be re-read as **"1 AI customer (Anthropic 34.5%) + 1 government (16.6%)"**. The 90-day termination clause of the Google contract (reported) stands, but it concerns a customer under 10%. Remaining open item: direct reading of the S-1 original sentence (size limit exceeded) — if the original differs, this is reverted (Source: table above · [November issue 1-4](2026-11.md) · `state.rule_proposals_not_applied[4]`).

**By-product of the correction — A-2032-1 measurement**: Government revenue = Customer A share × consolidated revenue. 3Q26 **$2,419M** (formula: 0.166 × 14,575) · 3Q25 **$1,333M** (formula: 0.239 × 5,576 — sum of 3Q25 revenue across three segments 3,097 + 813 + 1,666) → **+81%** (formula: 2,419 ÷ 1,333 − 1) · FY2025 **$3,903M** (formula: 0.209 × 18,674) · annualized **about $9.7 billion** (formula: 2,419 × 4) vs milestone $20 billion (2032). This measure is a "single customer above 10% (US federal government)", so it is a **lower bound** that excludes foreign government and military revenue, and if the share falls below 10% it disappears from the table and the series breaks — at that point we switch to the 10-K's annual government revenue description (S-1 style). The verdict rests on 2032 annual results; for now it is **undecided → in progress** (Source: ① [10-Q R12](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R12.htm) · [8-K Ex.99.1 3Q26](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066482/spaceexplorationtechnologi.htm) · `state.kpi_history[3Q25]` · [spacex-ipo-dashboard](https://spacex-ipo-dashboard.vercel.app/)).
